# Airbnb reviews: how to automate requests, responses, and review insights


by


[Guesty Marketing Team](https://www.guesty.com/blog/author/guesty-marketing-team/)

Every checkout starts a 14-day clock. In that window you nudge the guest, review them, and reply to whatever lands on your listing. Do it by hand for every stay and the work never ends. Automate the repetitive parts, keep your judgment for the reviews that need it, and stay inside Airbnb’s rules.


Higher ratings pay. AirDNA’s 2025 data shows listings rated 4.9 stars or higher earned 11% higher ADR and 15% more RevPAR ([AirDNA](https://www.airdna.co/blog/hosts-guide-to-airbnb-ratings) ).


**TL;DR**


- Guests and hosts each get 14 days after checkout to review, and reviews publish when both are in or the window closes.
- Automate the timing of review requests and the first draft of your responses. Keep a human on critical reviews.
- Never trade anything for a review. Airbnb’s Reviews Policy bans incentives and pressure.
- Read your private category ratings for patterns, then fix the cause behind the comment.
- Guesty® is a vacation rental software that automates review collection after checkout, uses AI review agents to draft personalized responses and surface recurring guest complaints, and turns a review that flags damage or cleanliness into a maintenance task.


## How do Airbnb reviews work for hosts?


Airbnb reviews follow a fixed window: on the day of checkout, Airbnb prompts both the guest and the host to review, and both have 14 days after checkout to submit. An Airbnb review is posted only after both parties submit or once the 14-day period ends, whichever comes first ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/13) ).


The rest of the rules shape what you automate:


- **Six categories plus an overall score.** Guests rate cleanliness, accuracy, check-in, communication, location, and value. Airbnb scores the overall rating as a separate category rather than averaging the other six ([Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/1257) ).
- **Three reviews to show a rating.** Your listing rating is the average of overall rating scores, and it appears once the home has at least three reviews.
- **Category scores are private.** Individual subcategory ratings and notes to the host are visible only to you and Airbnb.
- **No review for early cancellations.** A reservation canceled before the day of check-in can’t be reviewed by either side.


Airbnb may also use review information in search results, so[your ratings affect how often your listing gets seen](https://www.guesty.com/blog/how-to-earn-and-maintain-superhost-status/) and booked.

## How do you automate the review process and encourage positive guest feedback?


To[automate the Airbnb review process](https://www.guesty.com/blog/guide-to-airbnb-automation/) , use vacation rental software with automated messaging to time and personalize a post-stay review request around checkout. Airbnb already prompts guests on checkout day, so your message supplements that prompt, and Airbnb’s[Reviews Policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2673) bans incentivizing, pressuring, or trading anything for a review.


### Fix problems before checkout


Low stars usually start mid-stay. Airbnb names accuracy and cleanliness as some of the most common reasons guests give fewer than five stars ([Airbnb Resource Center](https://www.airbnb.com/resources/hosting-homes/a/how-to-handle-a-bad-review-376) ). A mid-stay message asking how things are going catches problems early. A broken coffee maker replaced on day two rarely makes the review. Make your[checkout instructions](https://www.guesty.com/blog/vacation-rental-checklist-for-checkout/) clear, too, since checkout is the last thing a guest does before Airbnb asks for a review. In Guesty, write Airbnb check-out instructions on the listing and sync them to Airbnb.


### Time the request around checkout


Schedule one automated post-stay message for checkout day or the next morning. Add one reminder later in the window, at most. More reads as pressure. Skip the request entirely for any stay with an unresolved complaint.

### Write a request that stays inside Airbnb’s rules


Keep it short and specific.


> Thanks for staying with us, Maria. We hope the hot tub was the highlight. Airbnb will ask you to review your stay, and your feedback helps the next guests know what to expect. If anything wasn’t right, message me directly so I can fix it.


The private-message line matters because it gives an unhappy guest somewhere to vent before the public version. Never include:


- A discount, refund, gift, or credit tied to the review
- A request for a specific star rating
- An offer to trade a positive review of the guest for one of your listing


Write your own review of the guest early in the window, while the stay is fresh, and stick to facts.


## How to respond to Airbnb reviews at scale


Post a public response to any review left for you. The response goes live immediately and appears on your listing page with the original review. Reply from Profile > Reviews > Reviews about you, or from Insights ([Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/32) ). Airbnb generally doesn’t mediate disputes over review accuracy, so your response is your side of the story.


### A reply structure for five-star reviews


Thank the guest by name, repeat one thing they loved, and invite them back. “Thanks, Dev. Glad the porch swing earned its spot in your review. The cabin’s yours whenever you want it again.”


### A reply structure for critical reviews


Airbnb’s own advice: thank the guest and share how you’re improving. Name the issue without arguing, state what you changed, and stop. “Thanks for the honest review. You’re right that the second bedroom ran hot. We’ve installed a ceiling fan and a portable AC unit.”


### Let AI draft, you approve


Responding is where hours disappear, and it’s where[Guesty’s AI agents](https://www.guesty.com/features/ai-for-short-term-rentals/) earn their keep. Review agents analyze guest sentiment and generate personalized responses, and the Negative review challenger classifies appealable negative reviews and drafts a targeted removal email. Every AI tool inside Guesty is trained on over 10 years of data from hundreds of thousands of listings.


Automated replies to five-star reviews are low risk. A one-star review about a safety issue is not. Read every critical draft yourself.


### When to request removal instead of replying


Request removal only when a review breaks the Reviews Policy: fake, not first-hand, incentivized or coerced, retaliatory, or against the Content Policy. A harsh star rating alone doesn’t qualify. Attach supporting documentation, and expect a decision by email, usually within 48 hours ([Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/3582) ).


## Your private category scores are the early warning


Guests can’t see your subcategory ratings. You can. Read them by category and by month. If check-in slips while every other score holds, look for the cause in the written reviews. Three guests mentioning a hard-to-find lockbox is a pattern.


A guest mentions a loose deck railing in a four-star review. The reply goes out the same day. The railing stays loose for the next guest.


That gap between replying and fixing is where the[Review to task dispatcher](https://www.guesty.com/features/ai-for-short-term-rentals/) fits. When a review flags damage, odor, or cleanliness, it creates a mandatory maintenance task and temporarily removes the disputed amenity. One Guesty customer described the payoff:


> “Best of all, the review list surfaces guest issues and conflicts instantly so we can take immediate action.”


*Freedom & Fortune, Sacramento, United States*


## What solutions are available for new hosts to automate guest reviews?


Hosts have three kinds of solutions to automate guest reviews on Airbnb: Airbnb’s built-in tools, vacation rental software that automates post-stay messages and review collection, and AI review agents that draft responses and turn complaints into tasks.


- **Airbnb’s built-in tools.** The checkout-day review prompt and category ratings in Insights. You still write every response and spot every trend yourself.
- **Vacation rental software.**[Automated messaging](https://www.guesty.com/features/automation-tools/) sends the review request on time for every stay, and a[unified inbox](https://www.guesty.com/features/unified-inbox/) keeps guest conversations in one place.
- **AI review agents.** Sentiment analysis, drafted replies, removal requests, and maintenance tasks created from review text.


In Guesty’s AI Gap report, a survey of 534 short-term rental operators, more than 50% save 1–4 hours a week using AI in their operations.


Reviews run as a loop: ask at the right moment, answer every review, and fix what guests keep pointing out. Guesty, a vacation rental software, runs that loop in one place, with automated review collection after checkout, AI-generated personalized responses, and complaints that become[maintenance tasks](https://www.guesty.com/features/tasks-management/) on their own. You keep the judgment calls and lose the copy-paste.
